blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Public Sector & Government, cloud, edge & platform engineering builds the runtime for everything else we do: hybrid and multicloud architecture, cloud-native modernization of legacy estates, edge and distributed infrastructure for latency-critical operations, sre and reliability engineering, internal developer platforms, finops, and mission-critical high-performance systems. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: hybrid & multicloud architecture, cloud-native & legacy modernization, edge computing & distributed infrastructure — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Twinverse with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Legacy mainframes as single points of failure
Tax, benefits and licensing cores run on platforms with shrinking talent pools; failure risk compounds annually.
Agency data islands
Benefits, tax, health and licensing systems never joined; citizens re-submit the same facts to every agency. Fraud and error hide in the seams.
Casework drowning in documents
Permits, claims and case files are paper-shaped; processing times measured in months erode trust and increase cost per case.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Procurement law and EU AI Act. Public-sector AI uses largely high-risk with conformity duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
